You will lead a small team of product engineers as a hands-on player-coach: shipping code yourself, unblocking others, and owning the health of both the product and the process. The core of the job is designing and running a development workflow where AI agents do a large share of the implementation work — and where human engineers remain firmly accountable for what ships. You will decide where agents are trusted, where humans must decide, and how we verify the difference.

How We Work

We believe AI changes what engineers do, not whether they matter. Agents write a lot of our first drafts; engineers define the work, review every change, run acceptance testing, and give the final greenlight on every commit and merge. Humans stay accountable for everything that ships. If that division of labor sounds right to you — ambitious about automation, uncompromising about verification — you will like it here.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the team. Manage, mentor, and grow a team of product engineers. Run planning, set the product engineering strategy, and keep delivery predictable.
  • Own the AI-native process. Define how work is decomposed into agent-runnable tasks: kickoff prompts, acceptance criteria, UAT checkpoints, and completion reports. Continuously refine what works.
  • Keep humans in charge of what matters. Establish clear human-decision points — PR approval and merge, commit sign-off, and user acceptance testing — so AI output is always verified by an accountable engineer before it lands.
  • Ship product. Design, build, and maintain features with AI native engineering.
  • Own data and integrations. Steward our database architecture and the integrations that connect us to schools — SIS rostering pipelines (OneRoster, Clever, ClassLink) that get the right students into the right classes with the right data.
  • Set the quality bar. Testing standards, CI checks, review discipline, and security practices appropriate for a platform serving a million students a year.
  • Measure and improve. Track where AI-assisted development helps and where it hurts. Kill process that slows the team down; scale what makes it faster and safer.

Skills, Knowledge and Expertise

  • 7+ years of professional software engineering experience, including 2+ years leading engineers as a team lead or engineering manager while remaining hands-on.
  • Strong full-stack depth with React and TypeScript in production, plus solid back-end experience with Node.js or similar.

At Zencoder.ai, we build and orchestrate AI agents that ship real work - code, research, operations, and more. What started as developer tooling is becoming a platform where people and agents collaborate across knowledge work tasks.

The Opportunity

We're looking for an experienced engineer to raise the bar on how our organization builds, tests, ships, and operates software - for both human engineers and AI coding agents.

This is AI harness engineering: the discipline of making the fundamentals (CI/CD, testing, IaC, observability, secure delivery) so solid and well-shaped that agents can work productively inside them. Developer experience and platform engineering are a subset of that work. When the harness is good, humans ship faster and agents stop getting stuck on things that shouldn't be hard.

Security is inseparable from this. AI agents are accelerating both the pace and the shape of vulnerabilities, and secure delivery has to be built into the same stream as everything else - not bolted on.

Product teams own their services, pipelines, and tests. Your job is to raise the ceiling across the org - defining standards, building leverage, and helping teams level up their workflows, tooling, infrastructure, security posture, and necessary changes for AI Agents.

Key Responsibilities

This is a hands-on lead role - you'll set direction and be deep in the code, infra, and pipelines yourself. A lead here is very much a builder.

  • Shape the platform and infrastructure that everything else runs on — the foundations product teams build on top of
  • Improve the full dev loop: local development, CI/CD, deployment, and production feedback
  • Define and drive standards around testing, IaC, observability, and secure delivery — and help product teams adopt them
  • Build shared tooling, templates, and golden paths that create real leverage — paved roads teams actually want to use
  • Own secure delivery end-to-end: unify security scanning, secrets management, dependency and supply-chain controls, and pen-testing workflows into the core pipeline so secure-by-default is the path of least resistance
  • Stay ahead of the shifting security landscape as AI agents reshape both how vulnerabilities emerge and how they're exploited

Overview

Believe in People? So Do We.

At Change Grow Live, we know that meaningful impact starts behind the scenes as much as it does on the front line.

Protecting personal data isn’t just a legal requirement it’s how we show respect, build trust, and honour the confidence placed in us by the people we support, our employees, and our partners.

We’re now looking for a Subject Access Request Coordinator to join our Legal Services Team.

Contract: This is a 12-month fixed term post.

Location: This is a national, home working role. Your base will be your nearest Change Grow Live office, and there may be opportunities to work from this location from time to time.Hours: Full Time, 37.5 per week

We are hoping to hold interviews for this vacancy week beginning 19th October 2026.

Responsibilities

About the Role

As a Subject Access Request Coordinator, you will be responsible for coordinating the administration of Subject Access Requests and supporting compliance with data protection legislation and organisational policies.

You will:

  • Coordinate and monitor Subject Access Requests and other individual rights requests, ensuring statutory deadlines are met.
  • Act as a key point of contact for requestors, managing correspondence and providing updates throughout the request lifecycle.
  • Coordinate information gathering activities with operational and central teams to obtain records within agreed timescales.
  • Support searches across electronic systems, email accounts and records repositories to identify and retrieve relevant information.
  • Maintain accurate records, case files, trackers and audit trails.
  • Prepare disclosure packs and supporting documentation for review by Data Protection colleagues.
  • Identify and escalate risks, delays or issues that could affect compliance.
  • Support the continuous improvement of SAR processes, templates, guidance and workflow systems.

  • Someone who is passionate about supporting individuals' rights, takes pride in handling sensitive information with care, and act as an advocate for good practice across the organisation.
  • Someone who is also highly organised, detail-oriented and able to manage a varied workload, working collaboratively with colleagues to ensure requests are handled accurately, fairly and within statutory deadlines.
  • Someone who enjoys bringing order to complex processes and wants to make a meaningful contribution to transparency, accountability and trust.

Why This Role Matters

Every day, people place their trust in Change Grow Live to handle their personal information appropriately.

By helping us manage Subject Access Requests effectively, you'll play an important role in ensuring transparency, accountability and compliance while supporting individuals in exercising their rights.

Our People Promise

At Change Grow Live, we are committed to creating an environment where people can do their very best work and feel valued for who they are and what they bring.

We focus on:

  • Creating the conditions for success for everyone who works and volunteers with us
  • Working together to deliver high-quality learning, development, and organisational growth

We recognise and value the contribution of our people, support wellbeing, and promote flexible and agile ways of working so that individuals and teams can succeed.

  • Where possible, we’re open to discussing working patterns that help you maintain a healthy work–life balance.
  • Enjoy discounts on shopping, cinema trips, holidays and more, along with our Refer a Friend scheme.

Meet Aperture

Aperture is a growth consultancy and advertising partner for ambitious apps, platforms and digital products.

We work across performance marketing, creative strategy, product optimisation, CRM, analytics and experimentation to help companies scale. Our clients rely on us to identify the biggest growth opportunities, turn them into well-designed experiments and deliver measurable commercial impact.

The role

We’re looking for a Monetisation Manager with deep, hands-on experience growing subscription-based mobile apps.

You will lead monetisation strategy and experimentation across a portfolio of clients, working across onboarding, paywalls, pricing, plans, trials, offers, product gating, retention and cancellation.

You must have personally configured and run experiments in both RevenueCat and Adapty, understand how the platforms work in detail and be confident diagnosing problems when the data or implementation does not behave as expected.

You’ll combine commercial thinking, customer understanding, product analytics and rigorous experimentation to help clients increase revenue without sacrificing retention or long-term value.

Requirements

What you’ll own

  • Audit clients’ monetisation models, subscription infrastructure, funnels, analytics and experiment history, then build prioritised roadmaps.
  • Personally configure and manage products, entitlements, offerings, paywalls, placements, audiences, targeting and experiments in RevenueCat and Adapty.
  • Lead experimentation across pricing, plans, trials, offers, onboarding, paywalls, product gating, localisation, cancellation and web-to-app journeys.
  • Design rigorous tests with clear hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, audiences, traffic allocation and decision criteria.
  • Analyse the full subscription funnel, from conversion and trial-to-paid through renewal, churn, revenue and LTV, identifying misleading results and meaningful differences between cohorts.
  • Reconcile data across RevenueCat, Adapty, the app stores, product analytics, attribution platforms and warehouse data, resolving tracking or implementation issues with technical teams.
  • Turn behavioural data, customer research and commercial insight into stronger propositions and experiments, working with design, product, engineering, analytics and CRM teams to launch and QA them.
  • Present clear recommendations and results to clients, documenting every experiment and contributing reusable learnings to Aperture OS.

What we’re looking for

  • Significant experience monetising consumer subscription apps across iOS and Android, with a proven impact on conversion, revenue or retention.
  • Deep, hands-on expertise in RevenueCat and Adapty, including personally configuring subscription products, paywalls and experiments.
  • Strong knowledge of App Store and Google Play subscriptions and rigorous A/B testing, from experiment design and sample size through to revenue maturity.
  • Excellent analytical and commercial judgement, including the ability to interpret funnel data, distinguish short-term conversion gains from genuine LTV growth and diagnose tracking issues.
  • Clear, confident client communication and a proactive approach to managing multiple workstreams, dependencies and blockers.

Particularly valuable experience

  • Superwall, Purchasely or similar monetisation platforms.
  • Product analytics tools such as Amplitude, Mixpanel, Firebase or PostHog, plus SQL or event-level analysis.
  • Web-to-app monetisation, localisation, cancellation flows and churn reduction.
  • Working across multiple clients in a consultancy or agency environment.

What success looks like

Within your first few months, you will have:

  • Established clear monetisation baselines and prioritised experimentation roadmaps for your clients.
  • Launched rigorous tests through RevenueCat and Adapty across pricing, paywalls, onboarding and retention.
  • Improved the reliability of monetisation data and the quality of experiment decisions.
  • Turned results into actionable recommendations and reusable learnings for clients and Aperture OS.

How we work

  • Client success is our success.
  • We take ownership of outcomes and raise blockers early.
  • We use evidence to make decisions and focus on measurable impact.
  • We communicate directly, thoughtfully and without ego.
  • We document what we learn so every experiment makes the next one smarter.

Why this role

Veradigm is looking for a Zuora architect to own how we quote, bill and collect. That covers the full flow from Salesforce CPQ to Zuora Billing to Kantata, our Professional Services platform. This isn't a maintenance role, and it isn't a design-only role. You'll decide how the pieces fit together and then build them yourself.

  • You own the architecture, and you build it. Catalog design, billing models, Workflows and integrations are your decisions, and you'll do the hands-on work to deliver them.
  • There's real modernization ahead. You'll rebuild the product catalog, consolidate multiple Zuora tenants into one, and help shape a possible move from Salesforce CPQ to Revenue Cloud.
  • You'll teach by doing. You'll work side by side with our Zuora administrators and help them grow, alongside Salesforce CPQ specialists and engineers on Boomi, Kantata and Workday.
  • Leadership sees the work. Billing accuracy affects revenue, so this work gets reported up and funded.

What you'll do

  • Design and build the Zuora product catalog: Products, Rate Plans, Charges and Amendments
  • Write and maintain Zuora Workflows, API calls and scripts yourself, including orchestration, error handling, retry logic and monitoring
  • Own the end-to-end quote-to-cash flow from Salesforce CPQ through Zuora Orders, working directly with the Salesforce and integration teams
  • Configure billing for subscription, usage-based and milestone models across the full subscription lifecycle: new sales, amendments, renewals and cancellations
  • Own the Zuora–Kantata integration for Professional Services billing
  • Troubleshoot and fix production billing issues directly
  • Mentor Zuora administrators through pairing, code and configuration reviews, and runbooks they can use on their own

What you bring

Required:

  • 8+ years in billing or quote-to-cash systems, including 5+ years hands-on with Zuora Billing: Orders, Workflows and the API
  • Served as the lead architect on at least two end-to-end Zuora implementations or major redesigns, owning the design from requirements through go-live

  • Deep command of the Zuora data model and product catalog design, including complex pricing across subscription, usage and milestone models

Big pluses, but we'll teach you the rest:

  • Building or maintaining a Salesforce CPQ → Zuora integration. This is the one we'd most like to see. If you haven't done it, experience with any CPQ platform, such as Zuora CPQ or Salesforce Revenue Cloud, also counts.

Senior Accountant, Finance Operations

About LeadSimple

LeadSimple builds software that helps property management companies manage sales and run their day-to-day operations. We care about clear communication, practical solutions, and owning the outcome.

About the role

We’re looking for a hands-on accountant to own our monthly close and keep our financial records accurate, current, and easy to understand. You’ll do the detailed work, follow discrepancies through to resolution, and give leadership a reliable view of the business each month.

Monthly accounting and reporting are the core of this role. You’ll also support a focused set of revenue operations tasks: keeping billing accurate, coordinating collections, preparing commission accruals, and making sure revenue data agrees across systems.

What you’ll own

Monthly close and financial reporting

  • Run the monthly close from start to finish, with a clear checklist, timeline, and ownership for every step
  • Prepare and post journal entries, accruals, and adjustments; maintain supporting schedules for revenue, deferred revenue, prepaid expenses, and other balance sheet accounts
  • Reconcile bank, credit card, and balance sheet accounts; investigate discrepancies and resolve outstanding items
  • Bring together accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll inputs, and expense records so the books are complete and correctly categorized
  • Prepare the monthly income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow reporting, with a concise explanation of material changes and unusual items
  • Keep documentation organized and reviewable, and coordinate with internal partners and outside accounting support to get missing information and close on time

Light revenue operations

  • Check customer billing against agreed terms and subscription changes; work with customer-facing teams to resolve errors
  • Maintain visibility into overdue receivables and coordinate follow-up with the people who own the customer relationship
  • Calculate and reconcile commissions and related accruals using approved compensation plans
  • Reconcile billing and revenue records across operational systems and the general ledger, and flag inconsistencies in recurring-revenue reporting

Make the process better

  • Document recurring work, reduce unnecessary manual steps, and build checks that catch problems before close
  • Surface financial risks and data gaps early, with a practical recommendation for resolving them

What success looks like in your first 90 days

  • You understand the accounting systems, recurring entries, revenue flows, and open reconciliation items
  • You own a documented close calendar and deliver accurate monthly financials on an agreed schedule
  • Key balance sheet accounts have clear supporting schedules, and unresolved items have an owner and a plan
  • Billing, collections, and commission workflows have simple, repeatable checks
  • Leadership can understand the monthly results and trust the numbers behind them

What you’ll bring

  • Experience personally owning month-end close and preparing financial statements
  • Strong working knowledge of accrual accounting, balance sheet reconciliations, and revenue recognition
  • The ability to trace a number from the source transaction through the financial statements and explain what happened
  • Confidence working in accounting software and spreadsheets, including reconciling data across systems
  • Careful judgment with confidential information and a habit of maintaining clear documentation
  • Crisp communication, dependable follow-through, and the initiative to solve problems without waiting to be asked

Especially useful

  • Experience with B2B SaaS or another subscription business
  • Familiarity with deferred revenue, recurring-revenue metrics, billing systems, and sales commission calculations
  • Experience improving a lean accounting operation and working with outside accounting partners

Help Build the Legal Foundation for the Quantum Era

Quantum computing could change how we discover drugs, design materials, secure communications, and solve problems no classical computer can. Rigetti is making that happen. We design and build superconducting quantum processors in our own fab and deliver quantum computing through the cloud and on-premises systems. We also work with leading government agencies, national labs, universities, and global enterprises to push the field forward.

The deals we sign now will shape how quantum computing reaches the world. We’re looking for the attorney who will lead them.

Why This Role

This is not a role maintaining someone else’s playbook. You’ll report directly to the VP, Legal, as a key member of a lean, high-impact legal team, working closely with Rigetti’s executive team and having real influence over how the company does business. You’ll have the opportunity to grow Rigetti’s commercial and government contracting function. That means designing the templates, processes, and negotiating positions the company scales on, and serving as a trusted advisor to leadership. As the business grows, the function you build will grow with it, and so will your role.

The work itself is unlike anything else in tech law. In a single week you might negotiate the sale of a quantum computer, structure a research collaboration on next-generation qubit materials, and advise on compliance in a government program. Many of these questions have never been asked before, and you’ll help answer them.

If you want your legal work to matter, not just to one company but to one of the defining technologies of this century, we’d love to talk.

      • Negotiate subcontracts and teaming agreements in both prime and subcontractor roles.

        • Train sales, BD, procurement, and program teams on contracting and government compliance.

    • J.D. and active membership in good standing in at least one U.S. state bar.

    • 7+ years of relevant experience, including meaningful time in-house.

    • A strong track record negotiating complex commercial agreements, ideally for hardware, semiconductor, deep-tech, or enterprise technology companies.

    • Hands-on experience with federal government contracts, including FAR/DFARS, subcontracting, and data rights.

    • A builder’s mindset. You enjoy creating structure where none exists and are energized, not overwhelmed, by a fast-moving environment.

    • Sound business judgment and the ability to explain legal risk clearly to engineers and executives.

      • Preferred

      • Law firm training combined with in-house experience.

      • Experience with OTAs, CRADAs, SBIR/STTR, and cooperative agreements.

      • Familiarity with EAR/ITAR as applied to transactions.

      • Experience with international transactions and public company work.

      • Curiosity about the technology.

Applications from women, minorities, and other under-represented groups are encouraged.

About Rigetti

Rigetti Computing is a pioneer in full-stack quantum computing. The company has operated quantum computers over the cloud since 2017 and serves global enterprise, government, and research clients through its Rigetti Quantum Cloud Services platform. The company’s proprietary quantum-classical infrastructure provides ultra-low latency integration with public and private clouds for high-performance practical quantum computing. Solutions Specialist

Where tech, process, and people actually meet — and we want you right in the middle of all three.

ABOUT US

Our professional services practice has been growing fast, and we’re looking for a Solutions Specialist to grow it with us. We work with clients across industries — from lean startups to established enterprises — helping them figure out what they really need, then making sure the solution actually sticks. We believe in doing things right: designing smart, building clean, and leaving clients better off than we found them.

AI is becoming one of the sharpest tools in our kit, and we’re excited about what it makes newly possible. We want someone who shares that excitement — and knows how to use it responsibly.

THE JOB

This role lives at the intersection of technology, process, and human experience. You’ll dig into client workflows, identify what’s really broken, design the right fix — and then make sure it actually lands. Some days that’s configuring a CX platform. Some days it’s building an AI-powered workflow. Often it’s both.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

▸ Solve for clients. Dig into workflows, pain points, and goals — then design and ship solutions that fit how teams actually work.

▸ Own the lifecycle. Support implementation from requirements gathering through configuration, testing, and go-live — keeping clients informed every step of the way.

▸ Be the calm in the change. Run working sessions, deliver hands-on training, and shepherd real adoption across organizations — including the folks who didn’t ask for any of it.

▸ Leave behind something useful. Create clear, practical documentation — playbooks, workflow diagrams, implementation guides — that clients keep using long after the engagement wraps.

▸ Think in systems, not band-aids. Spot friction and solve the root cause, not just the symptom. Design for scale.

▸ Stay endlessly curious. Keep up with new platforms, AI tools, automation, and CX innovation — and bring the good stuff back to sharpen what we deliver.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

▸ Curiosity that goes beyond the job description — you explore new tools for fun and have real instincts for where tech fits (and where it absolutely doesn’t).

▸ Genuine empathy — you think about how change feels for the people living through it, and you can guide someone through resistance with patience and clarity.

▸ Fluency in tech-meets-process — show you a workflow and you’ll see where it breaks, where it drags, and whether AI would genuinely help or just add noise.

▸ Experience working directly with clients or customers — support, success, implementation, or something adjacent.

▸ High EQ, accountability, and a sense of humor. You thrive solo and on a team.

jobs.description:
At Oversee, we build practical AI solutions for the $1.6 trillion global travel industry.

For over a decade, we have helped travel agencies and global enterprises cut travel costs and work more efficiently. Our AI-based reshopping products, FareSaver for air and HotelSaver for hotels, track booked trips and automatically rebook them when a better rate becomes available.

AgentSee, our agentic AI platform, works alongside travel agents. It reads traveler requests, handles bookings and changes, and takes on routine servicing tasks, so agents can manage more trips while improving service quality.

We work with the largest travel agencies and fortune 500 companies, supporting over $15B in annual booking volume for more than 11,000 customers in over 60 countries.

If you want to solve real problems with a focused team in a fast-moving market, Oversee is the place to build, grow, and make an impact.

Why join us?

This is the role that owns product marketing at Oversee.

You'll start with products that already work for a defined set of buyers, and your job is to work out who else they are for. That means real market research, sharper ICP definition, and evidence on where we have product-market fit rather than where we assume we do. What you find shapes our GTM strategy, it doesn't just describe it after the fact.

From there you own the message and everything downstream of it: positioning, persona and segment messaging, competitive and win/loss insight, and the language that runs through the website, campaigns, outbound and product surfaces. You'll write the product content that makes a technical capability legible to a commercial buyer, and you'll run launches end to end.

You'll report to the Marketing Director, with direct access to product, sales and the executive team. This is a function to build and own, not a queue of requests to work through.

Come shape the future of travel with us!

What you'll do:

Messaging and positioning

  • Refine and build on our existing positioning and messaging framework;
  • Own ICP, persona and segment messaging per product across corporate, leisure and partnerships;
  • Own product messaging across all markets and verticals;
  • Own the language that feeds every digital activity: website, campaigns, paid and organic, outbound sequences, product surfaces. One source, applied consistently, maintained as products change.

Market and competitive insight

  • Run standing competitive tracking across reshop and agentic AI for travel operations, corporate and leisure;
  • Run win/loss as a standing programme rather than a one-off project;
  • Run buyer research to sharpen segment understanding;
  • Produce market research and evidence on segment fit, with a recommendation attached.

Product content and copy

  • Write product-specific content: product pages, one-pagers, launch material, product-led blog content, and technical explainers;
  • Write and edit campaign copy in partnership with Growth Marketing;
  • Maintain a content cadence and strategy.
  • Onboard new reps on positioning and keep the existing team current as we ship;
  • Sit in on sales calls regularly and close the loop on what is working.

Launches and GTM

  • Build and run a repeatable, tiered launch process end to end, so effort matches materiality;
  • Coordinate cross-functionally so a launch lands as one motion;
  • Run post-launch measurement and retrospectives.

About you:

  • 7+ years in product marketing, in B2B SaaS, travel technology, or a comparable technical B2B environment;
  • A track record of owning positioning and messaging end to end, including the research behind it, not just executing a framework handed to you;
  • A strong writer who can produce product pages, battlecards, launch material and technical explainers without a copywriter in the loop;
  • AI-native. You use AI tools as part of how you produce work every day, not as something you have experimented with. This is a must-have;
  • Comfortable in a category-creation motion where there is no established playbook and the buyer does not yet have a name for the problem;
  • Experience working directly with sales: sitting on calls, building material reps actually use, and closing the loop on what works;
  • Able to take a technical product and make its value legible to a commercial buyer;
  • Self-directed. You can take a broad remit, sequence it yourself, and ship without being managed through it;
  • Native English speaker, based in the UK.

Experience marketing to travel agencies, TMCs, OTAs or tour operators is a strong plus, as is experience marketing AI or agentic products.

This role is remote within the UK.

As a Responsible AI Review PM for AG Consulting Partners, a typical day might include the following:

  • Reviewing Responsible AI (RAI) Impact Assessments and providing clear, actionable feedback based on HR Divisional Lead guidance and internal Responsible AI standards.
  • Evaluating AI-enabled systems, agents, and third-party technology implementations and making initial recommendations for approval or rejection, supported by compliance documentation and oversight.
  • Analyzing associated system deliverables (such as post-launch support plans, monitoring documents, and scope outlines) to ensure alignment with Responsible AI policies and best practices, such as fairness monitoring, human-in-the-loop safeguards, and abuse prevention.
  • Tracking engagement status and updates in the HR RAI Program Case Management Tool to ensure ongoing visibility and accountability across initiatives
  • Responding to inquiries from stakeholders across HR and the Responsible AI, Privacy, Legal, and Data Governance teams, offering thoughtful guidance and fostering a culture of ethical AI development.
  • Navigating complex or ambiguous compliance scenarios by driving clarity, prompting stakeholders to think analytically, and recommending risk-aware, scalable solutions—grounded in Responsible AI principles and policy expectations.
  • Collaborating cross-functionally with peers across the HR RAI team, the Office of Responsible AI, and other compliance functions to align on strategy and maintain high standards of AI governance throughout the lifecycle—from intake through post-deployment monitoring.
  • Applying project management best practices—balancing strategic thinking with attention to detail, ensuring strong communication, and proactively addressing blockers or risks
  • Quickly developing subject matter expertise on evolving AI compliance requirements by engaging with internal documentation, prior case reviews, and team mentorship.

  • Strong project management skills, including strategic thinking, attention to detail, and ability to manage timelines and cross-functional deliverables.

jobs.excerpt: Who we are:ShorePoint is a fast-growing, industry-recognized and award-winning cybersecurity services firm focused on high-profile, high-threat public and private sector customers who demand experience and proven security models to protect their data.
jobs.description:
Who we are:

ShorePoint is a fast-growing, industry-recognized and award-winning cybersecurity services firm focused on high-profile, high-threat public and private sector customers who demand experience and proven security models to protect their data. We embrace a “work hard, play hard” mentality and celebrate individual and company successes. We are passionate about our mission and going above and beyond to deliver for our customers, while fostering an environment that supports creativity, accountability, mission success, critical thinking and a desire to give back to our community.

The Perks:

As recognized members of the Cyber Elite, we work together in partnership to defend our nation’s critical infrastructure while building meaningful and exciting career development opportunities in a culture tailored to the individual’s technical and professional growth. We are committed to the belief that our team members do their best work when they are happy and well cared for. In support of this philosophy, we offer a comprehensive benefits package, major carriers for healthcare providers. Highlighted benefits include 144 hours of PTO, 11 holidays, 85% of insurance premiums covered, a 401(k), continuing education, certification maintenance and reimbursement and more.

Who we’re looking for:

We are seeking a Principal System Architect / subject matter expert (SME) to lead an enterprise Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) program for a federal agency and help establish the technical direction for transitioning from classical to quantum-resistant cryptography. This hands-on team lead role provides day-to-day direction to senior architects and engineers, supports workload coordination and partners with government stakeholders to advance PQC migration, crypto-agility and enterprise cybersecurity architecture. The Principal System Architect / SME position requires enterprise security architecture expertise, technical leadership and the ability to communicate complex program status, progress and value to technical teams and leadership. This is a unique opportunity to shape the growth, development and culture of an exciting and fast-growing company in the cybersecurity market.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Lead and technically supervise a team of senior systems architects and engineers, providing daily direction and mentorship.
  • Advise the project manager on workload distribution and staffing across the systems team.
  • Shape and support the agency’s PQC migration strategy in alignment with National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) post-quantum standards and Commercial National Security Algorithm (CNSA) 2.0 requirements.
  • Lead and conduct cryptographic inventory and discovery efforts to identify systems, protocols and data stores exposed to quantum decryption risk, including “harvest now, decrypt later” threats.
  • Establish crypto-agility standards to enable systems to transition between classical and post-quantum algorithms with minimal re-architecture.
  • Advise on hybrid classical/PQC implementation approaches to protect systems during the migration period.
  • Evaluate NIST-selected PQC algorithms, including ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA, for suitability across enterprise use cases, performance constraints and system requirements.
  • Gather and develop enterprise cybersecurity architecture requirements with federal stakeholders, building on analysis from information engineers.
  • Produce design architectures covering software, hardware and communications that meet current needs and anticipate future cross-functional requirements and interfaces.
  • Design, implement and baseline enterprise cybersecurity capability configurations.
  • Validate and verify capability implementations and ongoing configuration changes to confirm they meet intended security outcomes.
  • Develop policy aligned with Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) maturity models, including the Zero Trust Maturity Model and NIST standards while ensuring architectures remain compatible and compliant with industry and federal standards.
  • Foster collaboration across government and contractor teams to identify clear paths forward across key task areas.
  • Develop briefings, presentations and written deliverables that communicate program status, risk reduction and value to technical teams and agency leadership.

What you need to know:

  • PQC standards, including NIST-selected ML-KEM (FIPS 203), ML-DSA (FIPS 204) and SLH-DSA (FIPS 205) algorithms and the CNSA 2.0 suite and transition timelines.
  • Crypto-agility principles, hybrid cryptographic implementation strategies, public-key infrastructure (PKI), key management and certificate lifecycle management in the context of cryptographic modernization.
  • Enterprise cybersecurity architecture across software, hardware and network communications, including configuration baselining, validation and verification practices.
  • Federal cybersecurity frameworks and guidance, including NIST Special Publication (SP) 800-series publications, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework and CISA maturity models and how to translate federal policy and mandates into technical requirements and architecture decisions.
  • Enterprise network architecture and cryptography across segmentation, routing, secure transport protocols and supporting infrastructure components, including identity and access management systems, directory services, load balancers, firewalls and hardware security modules (HSMs).
  • Cloud, hybrid and multi-cloud security architecture, including Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), Software as a Service (SaaS), cloud key management, shared responsibility models, Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) requirements and cryptographic dependencies across applications, operating systems, firmware and third-party products.

Must have’s:

  • 10+ years of experience in systems architecture, including providing technical supervision and direction to senior architects and staff.
  • Active Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) or Certified Information Security Manager (CISM) certification.
  • Experience designing and implementing enterprise cybersecurity architectures and capabilities.
  • Experience developing enterprise cybersecurity architecture requirements with customers and stakeholders.
  • Experience baselining enterprise cybersecurity capability configurations and validating and verifying implementations and ongoing configuration changes.
  • Experience creating policy that adheres to CISA maturity models and NIST standards.
  • Experience with PKI, key management and certificate lifecycle management.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, build collaboration across stakeholders and communicate complex technical topics to technical and executive audiences through briefings, presentations and written deliverables.
  • Proven ability to analyze complex requirements and translate them into clear, actionable tasks and processes through critical thinking.
  • Applicants must currently be a U.S. citizen in compliance with federal contract requirements.

Beneficial to have:

  • Experience designing and implementing enterprise cybersecurity architectures that include PQC.
  • Hands-on experience with PQC standards, including ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA and CNSA 2.0 requirements.
  • Experience conducting cryptographic inventories and assessing “harvest now, decrypt later” risk exposure.
  • Hands-on experience piloting PQC or hybrid key exchange in TLS, VPN/IPsec, SSH or code-signing environments.
  • Experience with automated cryptographic and network discovery tools, including mapping cryptographic dependencies across large environments and building Cryptographic Bills of Materials (CBOMs).
  • Familiarity with FIPS 140-3 validation, HSMs and vendor PQC readiness roadmaps.
  • Familiarity with federal PQC policy drivers such as National Security Memorandum 10 (NSM-10), Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Memorandum M-23-02 and CISA PQC guidance.
  • Experience supporting cybersecurity work for federal government customers, including developing enterprise cybersecurity architecture requirements.
  • Experience implementing Zero Trust architecture in a federal environment.
  • Experience with major federal cloud platforms such as Amazon Web Services (AWS) GovCloud, Azure Government or Google Cloud for Government.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification.
  • Cloud security certifications such as AWS Certified Security - Specialty, Azure Security Engineer or Certified Cloud Security Professional (CCSP).
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, Engineering or a related field.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager
jobs.excerpt: Civica builds software that runs essential public services.
jobs.description:
Civica builds software that runs essential public services. Our systems support local government, the NHS, housing associations, and financial institutions: services that millions of people depend on every day. When our software works well, caseworkers make better decisions, clinicians access the right information, and councils deliver services that communities rely on.

We’re not a startup chasing the next hype cycle. We’re a company with deep roots in the public sector, working on problems that matter, and we’re investing seriously in how we build software to make sure we can keep doing that for the next decade.

Why we feel you'll like the role of Senior Engineering Manager

You’ll lead a domain of 6–10 teams (roughly 60–90 engineers), manage the Engineering Managers who run those teams day to day, and report to the Director of Engineering. It’s a manager-of-managers role, working alongside Product and commercial leadership as a peer, not just a bigger single team and not a purely internal-facing management job.

It’s a step up from an Engineering Manager role, not a bigger version of one. An EM owns a team. A Senior EM owns the system of teams: how they’re structured, how work flows between them, how the EMs leading them grow, and how the domain shows up to Product and the wider business. You’ll spend less time in any one team’s backlog and more time on the conditions that let several teams deliver well at once: resourcing, coaching, architectural alignment, and representing engineering credibly outside engineering.

The domain has real history and real constraints, not a green field: a mix of established and modernising systems, some legacy platforms alongside newer stacks, and teams at different levels of technical and operational maturity. You’ll be expected to form your own view of what’s working, what isn’t, and what needs to change, and to build the trust needed to act on it.

You’ll make decisions based on data, and help build a culture of measurement and continuous improvement.

What you’ll be accountable for:

Teams & people

  • Coaching and developing the Engineering Managers (and senior/lead engineers) who report to you: their technical judgement, their people leadership, their career growth.
  • Structuring and re-structuring teams as the work demands it, closing skill or capacity gaps and avoiding key-person dependencies rather than treating team shape as fixed.
  • Holding a consistent, visible bar for what a high-performing team looks like across your domain, and addressing sustained under-performance directly rather than leaving it to individual EMs.
  • Building a hiring and retention engine for the domain: enabling your EMs to hire well, and finding growth and mobility paths for strong engineers.

Delivery

  • Being the first line of escalation for delivery and technical issues across your teams, arriving with context and a proposed path forward rather than just the problem.
  • Coordinating effort across workstreams and delegating decisions to EMs with clear boundaries, then following through rather than disappearing after handoff.
  • Partnering with Product and commercial stakeholders to define shared metrics, challenge scope and trade-offs, and keep teams aligned to a durable mission rather than reactive requests.
  • Applying team-topology thinking (Conway’s Law and similar) to keep team boundaries and interaction patterns deliberate rather than accidental.

Technical craft

  • Staying close enough to the technical detail to ask good questions and spot drift, without being hands-on: your leverage is through your EMs and senior engineers, not your own commits.
  • Protecting space for quality against deadline pressure, and coaching your EMs to do the same with their teams.
  • Driving the domain’s operational maturity (testing, observability, incident response) in partnership with teams rather than mandating from above.
  • Building credible cases for structural or technical investment (replatforming, team re-formation, headcount) grounded in business need.

Leadership

  • Representing your domain to peers, Product, commercial stakeholders, and senior leadership, and representing the wider engineering organisation’s priorities back into your domain.
  • Operating as a genuine partner to senior stakeholders outside engineering, not just an escalation point they go through.
  • Challenging the status quo constructively, including with more senior colleagues, and forming clear, evidence-based views you’re willing to be challenged on.
  • Connecting your teams’ technical work to user and business outcomes.

Requirements

  • A track record of managing managers: you’ve led other Engineering Managers or equivalent senior technical leads, not just individual engineers, across a multi-team domain of comparable scale.
  • Strong technical grounding: not hands-on day to day, but deep enough to hold a real technical conversation, sense-check architectural direction, and know when to step in, across a mix of legacy and modern systems.
  • Evidence-based leadership: you use delivery and quality data to make decisions and build buy-in, including constructive challenge upward when the evidence supports it.
  • Genuine partnership with Product and commercial stakeholders: you can speak fluently about business and user outcomes, not just engineering output, and operate credibly as a peer to non-engineering senior stakeholders.
  • A coaching orientation: you develop people through delegation and follow-through, not by doing their job for them.
  • Comfortable with ambiguity: you create clarity for your teams even where the domain itself is still being shaped.

Nice to have

  • Experience in public sector, health, housing, or regulated environments.
  • Experience leading through team re-structuring or organisational change.
  • Exposure to legacy modernisation alongside greenfield delivery within the same portfolio.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted engineering practices and how they change what “good” looks like for a team.
  • Awareness of Developer Experience principles.
  • Worked in an environment where engineers own production services.
  • Experience working with globally distributed teams.

Benefits

Why You'll Love Working with Us
As a company, we're passionate about what we do and the citizens we serve. If you, too, want to champion the use of technology in public services to improve outcomes for citizens and public sector organizations, then Civica is the right place for you. We will help you unlock the best version of yourself, achieve career growth, and make a real difference to people and communities.

We know that when our people are happy, they work better and have greater job satisfaction. Here's what you can expect:

jobs.title: QA Tester
jobs.excerpt: About VantumVantum helps fractional operators win new clients while delivering for the clients they already have.
jobs.description:
About Vantum

Vantum helps fractional operators win new clients while delivering for the clients they already have. When you are managing several engagements, client work can consume the week and leave little time to find the next one.

The product is a web app for planning, tasks, calendar, goals, and Ask Vantum, an AI chat that helps an operator decide what to do next.

We are a team of five, working toward product-market fit. We are looking for a QA tester to use the live product the way a customer would, and to write bugs we can reproduce.

You will work directly with the founders.

What you will own

Your job is to find what is broken, write it so someone else can reproduce it, and check that the fix actually holds.

  • Walk the main flows. Sign-in, home, plan, tasks, calendar, goals, notes, and Ask Vantum.

  • Write each bug so it can be reproduced. Steps, what you expected, and what actually happened. Include the page, the account state, and a screenshot when it helps.

  • Recheck fixes. A bug is not done because someone said it was fixed. Confirm the original steps, and check that a nearby flow did not break.

  • Notice gaps. If a button does nothing, a save does not stick, or the page says one thing and the data shows another, file it.

  • Ask when a behavior might be intentional. Do not guess, and do not redesign the product.

You are not building features, and you are not writing production code. Clear written English is the job.

What we are looking for

You notice when software is wrong, and you can describe it without a developer sitting next to you.

You should be able to:

  • Follow a flow from start to finish. Include empty states, errors, and the second time through.

  • Write a bug report a stranger can follow. Steps, expected result, actual result.

  • Tell a display problem from a data problem. The page looks saved, but a refresh brings the old value back.

  • Show the evidence. Use a browser, screenshots, and a short screen recording when steps are hard to write.

  • Communicate clearly in written English. We read your reports every day.

  • Take ownership. Retest what you filed, and say when you cannot reproduce it.

Prior QA employment is useful. It is not required. Testing your own projects, a client product, or a careful write-up of bugs in software you use counts.

We do not need test automation, a computer science degree, or experience with our stack.

Why join

You will see real product decisions, talk to the founders, and watch your reports turn into fixes.

The work is part-time and remote. You set a steady weekly rhythm with us, and you tell us what you found in writing.

Compensation and working arrangements

  • $500 to $1,000 USD per month, depending on hours and how clearly you report what you find.

  • Part-time, remote.

  • At least three hours of weekday overlap with Bangkok (GMT+7), so we can review bugs the same day.

  • Hours are agreed on the call. This is not a full-time engineering role.

How we hire

1. Written application. We read how you describe a bug.

2. Screening call. We talk through a product you tested and a bug you filed.

3. A short look at the live app. You walk one flow and write up what you find.

Apply

Describe one bug you found that was easy to miss. Include the steps, what you expected, and what actually happened.

Tell us your timezone, your weekday overlap with Bangkok, when you can start, how many hours a week you can give, and your expected monthly pay.

jobs.description:
Are you ready to join a growing team that puts a premium on productivity and has an award-winning culture centered around transforming talented employees into effective business leaders? Then BHG Financial is the place for you.
In 2001, we started with an idea, an opportunity, and $25,000. Back then, our focus was strictly  on serving those in the medical industry. With healthcare in our heritage, we soon expanded  to serve high-earning professionals in many  other industries, providing all with leading-edge financial solutions, including our extensive network of community banks.
Today, BHG Financial has firmly established  its legacy as a leader in the financial services space. Founded on the philosophy of a better way to borrow, we are dedicated to helping accomplished professionals, small businesses, and institutions build upon their success through innovative financial solutions, a hassle-free process, and personalized concierge service.
Our relentless commitment to the success of our customers is part of what has made BHG Financial thrive. We take a 360-degree view of our customers to tailor the best solutions for their financial aspirations. Today's professionals have multiple sources of income, not just their paycheck. Therefore, it is essential to factor those in when making responsible lending decisions. Our continued focus on data, analytics, and proprietary modeling has enabled faster funding for our customers.
From business to personal loans to relationships with community banks, the country’s top professionals and business owners rely on us for our exceptional financial solutions and concierge service to continue their success and legacy.

Who You Are

You are a motivated Database Administration professional who is passionate about ensuring secure, reliable, and high-performing database environments across cloud and on-premises platforms. You excel at database performance optimization, troubleshooting, and operational excellence, and have extensive experience administering SQL Server and MongoDB databases, implementing high-availability solutions, and supporting complex database infrastructures. You are a detail-oriented, analytical, and proactive problem solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment where you can drive database stability, strengthen security and compliance, and continuously improve system performance through automation and innovation.

What You'll Do

  • Administer and optimize SQL Server instances across on-premises and Azure environments (SQL Database, SQL Managed Instance); perform capacity planning, performance tuning, index optimization, and query analysis
  • Manage MongoDB Atlas clusters and implement security policies, backup and recovery, replication strategies, and performance optimization for document-based workloads
  • Design and implement high-availability and disaster recovery solutions using Azure SQL Failover Groups, Distributed Availability Groups, and cross-platform replication
  • Lead database security initiatives: enforce RBAC, encryption at rest and in transit, audit logging, and compliance with financial services regulations
  • Automate operational tasks through T-SQL scripting, PowerShell
  • Manage monitoring and alerting infrastructure; analyze performance metrics and proactively identify optimization opportunities
  • Support backup/restore operations, and database migration projects
  • Other duties as assigned.

What You'll Need

  • 8+ years of hands-on SQL Server database administration experience; 3+ years with Mongo databases
  • Proficiency in Azure SQL Database and SQL Managed Instance administration and optimization
  • Strong MongoDB Atlas expertise: cluster administration, backups, query optimization, security configuration, and operational best practices
  • Ability to leverage the Atlas CLI to deploy and modify clusters programmatically; profiling slow queries, building efficient indexing strategies, and restructuring document schemas
  • Advanced T-SQL skills: stored procedures, triggers, query optimization, index tuning, and performance analysis
  • Experience with high-availability solutions: Availability Groups, Failover Clustering, or equivalent cloud-native alternatives
  • Proficiency in PowerShell scripting for database automation and infrastructure management
  • Knowledge of database security: column-level encryption, row-level security (RLS), transparent data encryption (TDE), and audit frameworks
  • Hands-on experience with database backup and recovery strategies, including BACPAC and bulk export/import operations
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex database performance issues and implement optimization strategies
  • Travel requirement: All roles require travel during the first 6 months of employment to attend the BHG Oars in Experience. After the initial 6 months, ongoing travel is expected at approximately ~5% annually for periodic team on-sites, team meetings, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Work Authorization: This role is not eligible for employer-provided immigration sponsorship. To be considered, applicants must already possess valid U.S. work authorization that will not require sponsorship now or in the future.

    • Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with other cloud database platforms: Azure Databricks
  • Proficiency with database monitoring tools: Redgate, Fog light, Azure Monitor, or similar platforms
  • Experience with SSIS (SQL Server Integration Services) or similar ETL tools
  • Knowledge of financial services compliance requirements (SOX, PCI, GDPR)
  • Certifications: Microsoft Certified Data Administrator (AZ-104), Azure Database Administrator Associate (DP-300), or MongoDB Certified DBA

Life at BHG Financial

At BHG Financial, we work hard and aren’t afraid to take risks. Since the beginning, our core values of PMA (positive mental attitude), team player, and loyalty have been the driving force behind every interaction we have between each other and our customers. We have a healthy respect for the daily grind, yet we value work/life balance. We believe that all employees should have the opportunity to lead and that good ideas can come from anyone. From the top down, our leaders are actively involved not only in strategic oversight and running the business, but also in the well-being and growth of all employees. We consider people our #1 asset, and help employees realize their full potential, set and exceed their goals, and explore new opportunities for personal and professional development.

Why You Should Join BHG Financial

We strive to offer amenities, opportunities, events, and programming that support the interests of our teams, while furthering the culture that makes us Great Place to Work® certified. Some of the benefits you can expect when you join BHG Financial include:
•Medical/Rx/Dental/Vision coverage for employees and their eligible family members
•Competitive PTO and vacation policies
•1 Friday off each month for Wellness Weekends
•Company 401(k) plan with employer contributions after one year
•Company-sponsored training and certification opportunities
•Quarterly award ceremonies where top achievers are celebrated and receive additional bonuses
•Ongoing volunteer opportunities to give back to the community through our BHG Cares program
If you’re ready for a career where you can exercise your passions, be surrounded by co-workers who are relentlessly committed to service, and have a team-player mindset, apply today!
BHG Financial is committed to equal treatment and opportunity in all aspects of recruitment, selection, and employment without regard to gender, race, religion, national origin, ethnicity, disability, gender identity/expression, sexual orientation, veteran or military status, or any other category protected under the law. BHG Financial is an equal opportunity employer; committed to a community of inclusion, and an environment free from discrimination, harassment, and retaliation.

Who we are:

Motive empowers the people who run physical operations with tools to make their work safer, more productive, and more profitable. For the first time ever, safety, operations and finance teams can manage their drivers, vehicles, equipment, and fleet related spend in a single system. Combined with industry leading AI, the Motive platform gives you complete visibility and control, and significantly reduces manual workloads by automating and simplifying tasks.

Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers – from Fortune 500 enterprises to small businesses – across a wide range of industries, including transportation and logistics, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, food and beverage, retail, and the public sector.

Visit to learn more.

About the Role:

Motive is looking for a Senior Commissions Forecasting & Sales Compensation Program Lead. The primary responsibility is to own the commissions modeling, forecast and related analysis in an FP&A-partnering planning process: establish the methodology, maintain the model, collect and validate inputs, produce forecast submissions, explain variances, and provide decision-ready commentary to Finance and business leadership.

The role also assists in designs, operationalization, and continuously improving global sales compensation programs. It sits at the intersection of FP&A, Sales, GTM Strategy and Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Payroll, and Business Technology.

The successful candidate will turn complex business objectives into a reliable, explainable commissions forecast and clear, scalable, auditable compensation programs. They will own the commissions forecasting process, including the forecast calendar, model architecture, assumptions, run-rate methodology, headcount and plan-change inputs, source-data validation, forecast submissions, actuals-to-forecast analysis, forecast-to-plan analysis, and executive-ready commentary. They will also evaluate plan mechanics, identify unintended incentives or payout risk, build analytical models, document policy intent, lead cross-functional decisions, and ensure approved changes are translated accurately into systems, communications, and operating processes.

This is a high-impact individual-contributor role for someone who can move comfortably between FP&A forecasting, strategic design discussions, detailed modeling, policy language, system requirements, and field-facing explanation. This role partners closely with our GTM & Corporate FP&A teams along with our Sales Operations teams. The role must understand how plan mechanics, headcount, attainment, hiring timing, ramping, quota changes, and payout behavior affect forecast accuracy, cost, seller behavior, payout experience, and operational risk.

What You'll Do:

  • Own the end-to-end commissions forecast process in partnership with FP&A and sales ops, including forecast calendar, model structure, assumptions, source data, submissions, and change control.
  • Produce monthly, quarterly, and annual commissions forecasts and explain actuals-to-forecast and forecast-to-plan variances by segment, role, plan component, headcount movement, attainment, and timing.
  • Establish forecast inputs and operating rhythms with Sales Ops, Finance, People, Payroll, and business leaders; document ownership, deadlines, assumptions, and evidence.
  • Assist in the design and evolution of sales compensation plans across multiple segments, roles, geographies, and pay periods.
  • Translate GTM strategy into measurable compensation mechanics, including quotas, crediting rules, accelerators, kickers, draws, SPIFFs, MBOs, ramping structures, and exception frameworks.
  • Build models and scenario analyses to evaluate plan outcomes, behavioral incentives, fairness, payout volatility, cost implications, and implementation complexity.
  • Partner with Sales Leadership, GTM Strategy and Operations, Finance, People, Legal, Payroll, and Business Technology to align on requirements, tradeoffs, approvals, and timing.
  • Co-own the compensation-design workstream for major programs such as annual-plan redesigns, new-product incentives, role or segment changes, and compensation-system migrations.
  • Convert approved design decisions into clear business requirements, decision logs, process documentation, test cases, and implementation-ready specifications.
  • Review system outputs and reporting for alignment to policy and intended plan behavior; identify root causes when results are inaccurate, delayed, or difficult for sellers to understand.
  • Establish practical governance for plan changes, exceptions, approvals, and effective dates, with a clear audit trail.
  • Create and deliver enablement for sales leaders, managers, and compensation partners; explain complex mechanics clearly and confidently.
  • Develop recurring performance reporting on attainment, payout behavior, plan participation, exception themes, forecast accuracy, and compensation-program effectiveness.
  • Partner with FP&A on forecast submissions, executive commentary, scenario analysis, and reconciliation of forecast assumptions to approved plan design and operating data.
  • Improve the seller and manager experience through clearer plan documents, better statements, self-service resources, office hours, and better intake processes.
  • Support audit and IPO-readiness activities by ensuring that plan logic, approvals, controls, and evidence are complete and reusable.
  • Mentor analysts and collaborate with systems and operations partners without having formal people-management responsibility.

What We're Looking For:

  • 6+ years of experience in FP&A, sales compensation, incentive compensation, sales operations, revenue operations, finance, or a closely related analytical discipline, including meaningful ownership of commissions or variable-compensation forecasting.
  • Demonstrated experience designing or materially changing sales compensation plans in a complex, multi-segment organization.
  • Strong FP&A, analytical, and financial-modeling skills; able to work comfortably with large datasets and build transparent forecast, bridge, variance, and scenario models.
  • Deep understanding of compensation mechanics such as quota allocation, attainment, crediting, accelerators, kickers, draws, ramping, clawbacks, SPIFFs, and exception handling.
  • Experience partnering with FP&A and senior stakeholders and building consensus across Sales, Finance, Operations, People, and Technology.
  • Ability to write clear policy language, business requirements, process documentation, and executive-ready recommendations.
  • Strong systems orientation and experience with an incentive compensation management platform such as Xactly, Varicent, CaptivateIQ, Everstage, Anaplan, or an equivalent system.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills, including the ability to explain complex compensation mechanics to non-specialists.
  • High ownership, attention to detail, sound judgment, and comfort operating in ambiguous, high-change environments.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience supporting a global SaaS, technology, or subscription business.
  • Experience with Salesforce, Workday, Snowflake, SQL, or business-intelligence tools.
  • Experience designing compensation for both new-logo and account-management organizations.
  • Experience creating enablement programs, compensation hubs, FAQs, or self-service resources.

jobs.excerpt: OverviewThe Social Media Content Strategist is responsible for supporting the development, execution, optimization, and growth of social media content across multiple brands and platforms.
jobs.description:
Overview

The Social Media Content Strategist is responsible for supporting the development, execution, optimization, and growth of social media content across multiple brands and platforms. This role combines social media strategy, content planning, trend identification, audience development, creator coordination, publishing execution, and performance optimization to support brand awareness, engagement, and business objectives.

The ideal candidate is highly knowledgeable in social media platforms, content trends, audience behavior, and digital storytelling. They will be responsible for identifying content opportunities, supporting content creation initiatives, managing social publishing activities, monitoring performance, and helping ensure content is optimized for maximum reach, engagement, and effectiveness across all social media channels.

Responsibilities

Without restricting the generality of the above-stated basic functions, this position shall perform such duties and responsibilities as may be assigned including but not restricted to the following:

Social Media Strategy

  • Support the development and execution of social media strategies across multiple brands and platforms.
  • Identify opportunities to increase audience engagement, community growth, brand awareness, customer acquisition, and retention.
  • Ensure social media initiatives align with broader content, campaign, and business objectives.
  • Monitor competitor activity, platform developments, and industry trends to identify growth opportunities.

Content Planning

  • Assist in the development and management of social media content calendars.
  • Coordinate content requirements across campaigns, product launches, promotional initiatives, and seasonal programs.
  • Support content planning activities by identifying content gaps, opportunities, and priorities.
  • Ensure content plans align with publishing schedules and campaign objectives.

Content Ideation & Trend Identification

  • Generate content ideas, campaign recommendations, social-first concepts, and platform-specific content opportunities.
  • Research emerging trends, creator content, viral formats, and audience interests.
  • Monitor cultural moments and platform developments that may support brand engagement.
  • Recommend new content formats and creative approaches that improve performance and audience engagement.

Content Publishing

  • Manage content publishing across social media platforms including Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, X, LinkedIn, Pinterest, and emerging channels as required.
  • Schedule and publish content according to approved content calendars and campaign plans.
  • Ensure content is properly formatted and optimized for platform-specific requirements.
  • Maintain publishing accuracy, quality control, and adherence to established workflows.

Platform Optimization

  • Optimize content for engagement, reach, retention, audience growth, and overall channel performance.
  • Ensure content follows platform best practices and current content trends.
  • Support content repurposing initiatives to maximize content value across channels.
  • Recommend improvements to publishing strategies, content formats, and platform execution.

Creator & Influencer Coordination

  • Support creator and influencer outreach initiatives.
  • Assist with creator identification, content planning, approvals, and publishing requirements.
  • Coordinate creator deliverables and content collection activities.
  • Ensure creator content aligns with campaign objectives and brand standards.

Audience Engagement

  • Monitor comments, messages, reviews, tags, mentions, and social media conversations across channels.
  • Engage with audiences in accordance with brand guidelines and community standards.
  • Escalate customer service concerns, compliance issues, or reputation risks when necessary.
  • Support initiatives designed to increase audience participation and engagement.

Community Insights

  • Monitor audience sentiment, engagement trends, and customer feedback.
  • Identify recurring audience questions, interests, and opportunities for future content.
  • Share audience insights with creative and content teams to improve content development.
  • Support social listening and competitive monitoring activities.

Performance Tracking

  • Monitor and analyze social media performance metrics including engagement, reach, impressions, views, audience growth, click-through rates, and conversions.
  • Evaluate content effectiveness across brands, campaigns, and platforms.
  • Identify top-performing content and opportunities for improvement.

Performance Optimization

  • Use social media analytics and audience insights to improve content performance.
  • Recommend adjustments to content formats, publishing schedules, creator initiatives, and channel strategies.
  • Support testing initiatives designed to improve engagement and audience growth.
  • Stay informed of algorithm updates, platform changes, and evolving best practices.

Reporting & Insights

  • Prepare regular social media performance reports and content summaries.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support campaign recaps, content audits, and performance reviews.
  • Demonstrate how social media initiatives contribute to broader business objectives.

Internal Collaboration

  • Work closely with content strategists, designers, videographers, editors, marketing stakeholders, and external partners.
  • Participate in campaign planning, content development, and creative reviews.
  • Ensure social media requirements are incorporated into content planning and production activities.

Content Production Support

  • Provide platform-specific recommendations during content planning and production.
  • Support content shoots, creator initiatives, product launches, and marketing activations when required.
  • Assist in preparing content for publication and distribution.
  • Ensure social media content aligns with approved creative direction and brand standards.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Digital Media, Advertising, Public Relations, Journalism, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.
  • 3+ years of experience in social media, content marketing, digital marketing, community management, or related fields.
  • Strong understanding of major social media platforms, content trends, audience development, and platform best practices.
  • Experience managing social media content calendars, publishing schedules, and platform execution.
  • Strong copywriting, communication, and content planning skills.
  • Experience utilizing social media analytics and performance data to guide strategic recommendations.
  • Familiarity with social media scheduling, publishing, listening, and analytics platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.

Preferred (Not Required)

  • Experience working with retail, e-commerce, cannabis, CBD, consumer packaged goods, or lifestyle brands.
  • Experience coordinating creators, influencers, contractors, or external content partners.
  • Familiarity with content production workflows including photography, videography, short-form video, and creator content.
  • Experience utilizing AI-powered tools for content ideation, planning, and optimization.
  • Knowledge of social listening, audience research, and trend monitoring tools.
  • Portfolio or examples demonstrating successful social media campaigns, audience growth initiatives, and content performance improvements.

About Us

High Tide Inc. is the leading community-grown, retail-forward cannabis enterprise engineered to unleash the full value of the world’s most powerful plant and is the second-largest cannabis retailer globally by store count⁷. High Tide (HITI) is uniquely-built around the cannabis consumer, with wholly-diversified and fully-integrated operations across all components of cannabis, including:

  • Bricks & Mortar Retail: Canna Cabana™ is the largest cannabis retail chain in Canada, with 195 current locations spanning British Columbia, Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario and growing. In 2021, Canna Cabana became the first cannabis discount club retailer in the world.
  • Retail Innovation: Fastendr™ is a unique and fully automated technology that employs retail kiosks to facilitate a better buying experience through browsing, ordering and pickup.
  • Consumption Accessories: High Tide operates a suite of leading accessory e-commerce platforms across the world, including Grasscity.com, Smokecartel.com, Dailyhighclub.com, and Dankstop.com.
  • E-commerce Platforms: High Tide operates a suite of leading accessory sites across the world, including Grasscity.com, Smokecartel.com, Dailyhighclub.com, and Dankstop.com.

CBD: High Tide continues to cultivate the possibilities of consumer CBD through Nuleafnaturals.com, FABCBD.com, blessedcbd.de and blessedcbd.co.uk.

Wholesale Distribution: High Tide keeps that cannabis category stocked with wholesale solutions via Valiant™.

Licensing: High Tide continues to push cannabis culture forward through fresh partnerships and license agreements under the Famous Brandz™ name.

High Tide consistently moves ahead of the currents, having been named one of Canada’s Top Growing Companies in 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024 by the Globe and Mail’s Report on Business Magazine, and was named as one of the top 10 performing diversified industries stocks in both 2022 and 2024 TSX Venture 50. High Tide was also ranked number one in the retail category on the Financial Times list of Americas’ Fastest Growing Companies for 2024.
